title: Tor amplitude of Rf_* for N-torsion complexes over a Noetherian ring
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $\Lambda$ a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a separated morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of quasi-compact $k$-schemes locally of finite type [def-weil-scheme-over-base, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $\dim X\le d$ for $d\in\mathbf N$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] be bounded constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] with Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ for integers $a,b$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude], and suppose $N\cdot\mathrm{id}_K=0$ for an integer $N\ge1$ invertible on $Y$. Then the module-sheaf derived direct image $Rf_*K$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$.

proof.text: Use the existing equivalence between the all-cohomology and t-structure definitions of Tor amplitude. The tensor-unit test gives K.IsGE a and K.IsLE b. Bounded constructibility also supplies boundedness for the constant projection theorem. If a > b, the standard t-structure implies K is zero; the additive derived direct image, tensor, and homology functors preserve zero, giving the entire conclusion in this case. In the remaining case a <= b.

proof.text: For every field extension s:Spec L -> Spec k, the existing source theorem topologicalKrullDim_pullback_le_of_field gives dim(X times_k L) <= dim X <= d. Transport along the canonical isomorphism from any cartesian square to this pullback. This supplies precisely the uniform field-extension hypothesis of the torsion abelian higher-direct-image theorem, with the same d. No local-dimension calculation is needed.

proof.text: Let F be a module sheaf whose underlying abelian sheaf is torsion. The torsion-abelian higher-image bound and step 2 show vanishing above 2d. The higher-direct-image forgetful comparison transfers this to the underlying abelian sheaf of the module higher direct image. Faithfulness of the additive forgetful functor detects zero via its identity morphism. The total-derived/plus single-object comparison gives the identical vanishing for H^q(Rf_*(F[0])); for positive q use q.toNat and the equality of its integer cast with q. In negative degrees, the existing left t-exactness theorem for Rf_* gives vanishing. This establishes the heart interval [0,2d] without any torsion-ring hypothesis.

proof.text: For any ordinary module M put E = K tensor^L M_X[0]. The Tor hypothesis gives its cohomology interval [a,b]. Additivity of tensorRight sends N id_K = 0 to N id_E = 0, and additivity of each homology functor gives the same annihilator on H^r(E). Evaluation at every etale object sends this identity to N x = 0 on every section, proving the underlying abelian cohomology sheaf is torsion since N is nonzero. Take S to be the class of module sheaves with torsion underlying abelian sheaf. It is invariant under isomorphism and contains zero. Apply bounded_heart_amplitude to Rf_*, this S, the heart interval [0,2d] from step 3, and E, obtaining vanishing of H^i(Rf_* E) outside [a,b+2d].

proof.text: For every geometric point of Y, exactness of its sheafFiber functor and its derived homology comparison carry the vanishing from step 5 to the derived geometric stalk. The constant-single tensor comparison identifies it with the tensor of the stalk of Rf_*K with M[0]. The first equivalence of geometricStalk_torAmplitude_test, with a <= b+2d, upgrades these ordinary-module tests at every geometric point to the full Tor interval for Rf_*K, tested against all module sheaves.
